answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Give the running legs a proper break first. For the next 7 to 10 days, walk only, and let the quads, blister and sleep come back to normal. Around day 10 to 14, try a 20 to 30 minute shuffle at a very easy effort; if nothing barks, add short easy runs every other day through early November.

The Thanksgiving 10K is possible but it is tight, and it only makes sense if recovery goes smoothly. A rough path, if you want to race it: walks this week, three or four short easy runs next week, then two weeks of normal easy running with a couple of light pickups, then a short taper. We should decide around Oct 28 based on how the body is responding, not on the calendar. If anything still feels off then, we treat it as a social run, not a race.

new.analysis:
You executed the race plan beautifully for 20 miles at about 8:32/mi, then the quads gave out and the last 10K drifted to 9:30/mi. That is a very common pattern in a second marathon, and it points at two things for next time: a bit more time on feet in the long runs, and more marathon-pace work inside them. None of that matters this month; it is a note for whatever we build next.

Right now the job is to let the damage repair. A marathon tears muscle fibers, drains glycogen and loads the tendons; running on top of that only slows the comeback. A classic guide is one easy day per hard racing mile before real training resumes, so think of the first two weeks as walking and very light movement, with running returning when the quads are quiet on stairs and the blister is closed.

The Thanksgiving 10K is where I want to be careful with you. Five weeks is on the short end, and chasing a time there risks turning a great marathon block into an injury. If you want to run it, let us plan on running it, not racing it: use it as a fun hard effort at about half-marathon effort, not an all-out 10K. We will revisit once you have two easy weeks in the bank.

Tell me what you would like the next block to point at. Options include a spring marathon with a sub-3:45 rematch, a winter half to sharpen speed, or a quiet base phase to build the aerobic engine before deciding. Your answer shapes November and December.

safetyCallouts.title: Blister care.
safetyCallouts.body: Keep it clean and covered, and if it reddens, spreads, weeps or gets more painful, see a pharmacist or doctor rather than running through it.

safetyCallouts.title: Quad pain that is not settling.
safetyCallouts.body: Marathon soreness should ease a lot by day 5 to 7; sharp, one-sided or worsening pain is different and worth a visit to a physio before you start running again.
